global_flags.-v: Verbose mode — prints more detailed output
global_flags.--verbose: Verbose mode — prints more detailed output
global_flags.-n: Dry-run — shows what would happen without doing it
global_flags.--dry-run: Dry-run — shows what would happen without doing it
global_flags.-y: Automatically answers yes to all prompts
global_flags.--yes: Automatically answers yes to all prompts
global_flags.-f: Force — skips confirmation and overwrites without asking
global_flags.--force: Force — skips confirmation and overwrites without asking
global_flags.-i: Interactive — asks for confirmation before each action
global_flags.--interactive: Interactive — asks for confirmation before each action
global_flags.-r: Recursive — applies to all files and subdirectories
global_flags.-R: Recursive — applies to all files and subdirectories
global_flags.--recursive: Recursive — applies to all files and subdirectories
global_flags.-p: Create parent directories as needed (mkdir) or preserve timestamps (cp/tar)
global_flags.-a: Archive mode — preserves permissions, timestamps, and copies recursively
global_flags.--all: Includes hidden files and shows all entries
global_flags.-l: Long format — shows detailed file information
global_flags.-s: Silent mode or shows file sizes depending on command
global_flags.-d: Target is a directory or dereference symlinks
global_flags.-x: Debug/trace mode — prints each command before executing
global_flags.-c: Specifies a command string to execute
global_flags.-u: Update — only copies when source is newer than destination
global_flags.-O: Specifies output file (wget) or saves with remote filename
global_flags.-k: Keep going despite errors, or insecure TLS (curl)
global_flags.-S: Suffix for backups or sort by size

rm.-r: Recursive delete — removes directories and all their contents
rm.-f: Force — no error if files are missing, never prompts
rm.-rf: Recursive + force — instantly deletes directories without asking
rm.-i: Interactive — asks before deleting each file
rm.-v: Verbose — prints each file as it is deleted
rm.--no-preserve-root: DANGEROUS: allows deleting the root filesystem /

chmod.-R: Recursive — changes permissions of all files in directory tree
chmod.-v: Verbose — outputs diagnostic for every processed file
chmod.-c: Like verbose but only reports when a change is made
chmod.777: All permissions to everyone — read, write, execute for owner, group, and others
chmod.755: Owner can read/write/execute; others can only read/execute (typical for dirs)
chmod.644: Owner can read/write; others can only read (typical for files)
chmod.600: Only owner can read/write; no access for anyone else

curl.-X: Specifies the HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.)
curl.-H: Adds a custom header to the request
curl.-d: Sends data in the request body (POST)
curl.-o: Writes output to a file instead of stdout
curl.-O: Saves file with the same name as the remote file
curl.-s: Silent mode — no progress bar or error messages
curl.-v: Verbose — shows full request and response headers
curl.--retry: Retries the request N times on failure

dd.if: Input file — the source to read from
dd.of: Output file — the destination to write to
dd.bs: Block size — how many bytes to read/write at a time
dd.skip: Skips N input blocks before starting
dd.seek: Skips N output blocks before writing

find.-type: Filters by type: f=file, d=directory, l=symlink
find.-mtime: Matches files modified N days ago
find.-size: Matches files of a specific size
find.-maxdepth: Limits search depth to N levels
find.-mindepth: Starts searching at N levels deep
find.-exec: Runs a command on each matched file
find.-delete: DELETES each matched file — cannot be undone

git.clone: Downloads a remote repository to a new directory
git.add: Stages files for the next commit
git.commit: Records staged changes to the repository
git.push: Uploads local commits to the remote repository
git.rebase: Replays commits on top of another branch
git.reset: Moves HEAD to a different commit (can lose work)
git.clean: Removes untracked files from the working directory
git.status: Shows the state of the working directory
git.checkout: Switches branches or restores working files
git.--hard: With reset: discards all uncommitted changes permanently

tar.-t: List contents of an archive without extracting
tar.-v: Verbose — list files as they are processed
tar.--strip-components: Removes N leading path components when extracting

ssh.-i: Specifies the private key file to use
ssh.-L: Local port forwarding — tunnels a remote port to your local machine
ssh.-R: Remote port forwarding — exposes a local port on the remote machine
ssh.-N: Does not execute a remote command (useful for forwarding)
ssh.-A: Enables SSH agent forwarding (use with caution)
ssh.-v: Verbose — useful for debugging connection issues
ssh.-X: Enables X11 forwarding for GUI applications

rsync.-a: Archive mode: preserves permissions, symlinks, timestamps, recursion
rsync.-n: Dry-run — shows what would be transferred
rsync.--delete: Deletes files in destination not present in source
rsync.-e: Specifies remote shell to use (usually ssh)

sed.-i: Edit files in-place (modifies the original file directly)
sed.-e: Adds a script to the commands to be executed
sed.-n: Suppresses automatic printing of pattern space
sed.-E: Uses extended regular expressions (same as -r on some systems)

ls.-l: Long format — shows permissions, owner, size, and date
ls.--color: Colorizes the output by file type
